one_line: Geophysics storefront where an agent reads a live VES brief, checks physical fit, compares instruments, and drafts a quote.
what_it_does: Combines a structured site brief with WebMCP tools for physical-constraint matching, comparison, and quote drafting while keeping submission human-controlled.
leverage_rationale: The structured agent surface can read unsubmitted shared state and apply domain constraints more reliably than UI-driving automation, though the core comparison outcome is still conceptually reproducible with a general agent.
leverage_evidence: Pitch explicitly says the agent reads the live unsubmitted VES site brief with no REST fallback.
About text describes typed physical-limit scoring, visible comparison-tray updates, and quote drafting.
Frame sheets show the Site Brief and Comparison Tray workflow, but not a fully evidenced quote submission.
execution_rationale: The packet coherently shows the brief-entry workspace and assistant interaction, but the visual evidence does not show completed instrument results or an end-to-end quote outcome.
execution_evidence: Frames show persistent GeoMart workspace, structured target depth/resistivity/terrain/budget fields, and assistant-generated brief content.
Devpost packaging shows the same Site Brief/Comparison Tray concept.
Comparison Tray is largely empty in much of the frame evidence and no final quote is visibly demonstrated.
impact_rationale: Geophysics survey practitioners have a specific, real need to match instruments to physical site constraints and budgets; the proposed workflow directly reduces manual cross-referencing and unsafe mismatches.
impact_evidence: About text identifies VES practitioners and 25 spec-sheet cross-referencing as the problem.
Pitch and form visibly center target depth, resistivity, terrain, and budget.
creativity_rationale: Applying shared WebMCP state to a specialized geophysics procurement decision, with physical constraint rejection rather than generic product search, is a memorable and well-motivated angle.
creativity_evidence: Domain-specific VES mismatch detection is distinct from the challenge's generic storefront example.
Human review and browser-resident unsubmitted brief are pursued as core interaction details.
usability_note: Structured brief and visible tray appear understandable, though the dense dark workspace and unshown final result limit confidence.
red_flags: No usable video evidence despite frame sheets; final quote/result is not clearly shown.
standouts: Strong domain grounding and explicit no-REST/shared-live-state thesis.
advance_reason: Strong differentiated concept and meaningful WebMCP delta; execution evidence is incomplete but coherent.

one_line: A repair-shop digital twin where an agent searches schedules and works the same floor state as a manager.
what_it_does: Provides board and isometric floor views, typed scheduling tools, seeded simulation search, and manager-controlled overrides for repair-shop planning.
leverage_rationale: Typed tools carrying scheduling context make the agent a participant in shared operational state rather than a fragile UI imitator; a general UI agent would be markedly less reliable for constraint-heavy replanning.
leverage_evidence: About text describes 13 typed tools, shared board state, schedule search across seeded runs, and agent catch-up after human moves.
Frames show a repair-floor/board interface with bays, vehicles, and operational status panels.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent product with two synchronized views, deterministic engine, manager controls, and visible floor workflow; the actual video is absent, so this remains claimed execution.
execution_evidence: Frames visibly show structured board/floor UI, bays, vehicles, and status/time elements.
Description states a deterministic seeded TypeScript engine and manager drag/lock controls.
Devpost packaging includes matching repair-shop visualization.
impact_rationale: Repair-shop managers have a concrete scheduling and exception-management problem, and shared agent assistance can reduce cognitive load while preserving accountability.
impact_evidence: About text identifies bay timing, parts slips, and manager gut-feel replanning.
Visible board includes multiple bays and operational plan indicators.
creativity_rationale: The agent-as-technician on a shared digital twin, with human authority and typed context rather than click imitation, is a fresh operational interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Project explicitly reframes agent as another team member on the floor.
Manager can make arbitrary changes and the agent understands the resulting trade-offs.
usability_note: Board and floor views communicate operational state clearly, though dense isometric detail may require onboarding.
red_flags: No submitted video; frame sheet does not independently prove agent invocation or schedule-search completion.
standouts: Strong shared-state framing and credible domain workflow.
advance_reason: High-quality concept with strong WebMCP leverage and coherent visible product packaging.

one_line: A shared medication list that gives caregivers and pharmacists role-specific agents with FDA-cited interaction flags.
what_it_does: Maintains one medication state, checks additions such as ciprofloxacin against existing prescriptions, and surfaces verbatim FDA-label evidence with role-aware tools.
leverage_rationale: The product's central value is shared human-agent state with distinct tool permissions and auditable structured evidence; ordinary UI driving would be unreliable and would not naturally preserve this collaboration model.
leverage_evidence: About text says caregiver and pharmacist links expose different WebMCP tool sets on the same list.
Frames show medication list, agent workflow, FDA/openFDA retrieval, and graph-like evidence paths.
The project explicitly keeps exact label sentences, set IDs, and source URLs attached to flags.
execution_rationale: The packet gives unusually detailed and consistent evidence of the core workflow, including list state, medication addition, interaction detection, role separation, and traceable source evidence; the 119-second video is represented by frames and packaging.
execution_evidence: Frames show the 11-medication dashboard and ciprofloxacin addition with warning state.
Frames show connected FDA/openFDA processing and caregiver-facing result UI.
Description specifies 64 drugs, 1,012 interaction sentences, and exact source linkage.
impact_rationale: Medication reconciliation for an older adult across caregivers, pharmacists, and multiple doctors is a high-stakes real problem; the demonstrated source-grounded warning directly addresses it.
impact_evidence: Narrative identifies an elderly patient, multiple prescriptions/doctors, remote caregiver, and missed warfarin/ciprofloxacin checking.
Frames visibly show a consolidated list and interaction-warning workflow.
creativity_rationale: Role-specific agents on one medication list plus verbatim-label evidence and disagreement as product behavior is an ambitious, memorable collaboration model.
creativity_evidence: Different windows intentionally expose different tools and authority.
Safety flags are tied to exact FDA label text rather than opaque summaries.
usability_note: The unified list and explicit evidence improve trust, though the density of clinical detail may challenge casual users.
standouts: Exceptional source-grounded safety workflow and shared role-specific state.
advance_reason: Top-tier impact, WebMCP leverage, and unusually complete evidence.

one_line: A commerce cancellation layer that requires effect approval and independently verifies the customer outcome before saying done.
what_it_does: Reads order truth, proposes exact fulfillment/order/payment transitions, gates commit on human approval, and performs a fresh verification read afterward.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP exposes structured current truth and valid resolution while the page owns approval and verification; this shared, stateful contract materially changes reliability compared with UI-driving agents that may report partial success.
leverage_evidence: Description separates projected effects, website-owned approval, commit, and fresh verification.
Frames visibly show order G1-ORDER-1001, state transitions, confirmation gate, and ProofDone verification panel.
execution_rationale: The central workflow is clearly coherent and visibly complete from order inspection through proposed resolution and verification, with explicit partial-failure semantics.
execution_evidence: Frames show AWAITING_PICK, NOT_YET_DISPATCHED, captured payment, proposed cancellation/refund transitions, and confirmation.
Final panels show an Order resolution/ProofDone state based on independently observed effects.
About text explains that refund failure is not reported as success.
impact_rationale: Commerce operators and customers have a real need for honest cancellation/refund outcomes across order, fulfillment, shipment, and payment systems; preventing false completion is directly valuable.
impact_evidence: Visible order workflow spans fulfillment, shipment, store order, and payment.
Project specifically addresses partial execution and captured payment risk.
creativity_rationale: Treating post-tool verification and earned completion as the product, rather than merely adding an action tool, is a novel and ambitious agent interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Human approval intentionally belongs to the website, not an agent tool.
Independent verification is a separate product phase and visible state.
usability_note: Explicit effects and confirmation support safe use; the multi-state terminology may be demanding for non-operators.
red_flags: No video submitted; frame sheets show product outcome but not direct agent invocation.
standouts: Strong safety contract around partial execution and verification.
advance_reason: Distinctive, high-impact WebMCP thesis with strong end-to-end visual evidence.

one_line: A co-op puzzle game where a human and an AI robot must coordinate because each can control only part of the solution.
what_it_does: Presents three jointly solvable levels, gives the agent six board/action/speech tools, and deliberately withholds any tool that could move the human character.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is the interaction medium that makes the agent a constrained teammate with shared board state; the missing human-control tool is essential to the game design and cannot be replaced by a comparable generic UI-driving solution.
leverage_evidence: Description states agent controls robot but cannot move the human, and a solver verifies human dependence.
Six tools cover read, move, hint, reset, level change, and speech while preserving asymmetric agency.
execution_rationale: The written packet gives strong implementation detail and a bounded three-level scope, but no frame sheet or video was submitted, so visual completeness and playability are not independently evidenced.
execution_evidence: Description specifies vanilla static implementation, joint-state BFS solver, and solvability tests.
No video frame sheets submitted; only packaging screenshot is available.
impact_rationale: Players seeking cooperative puzzle play have a clear entertainment and learning value, and the design creates genuine communication rather than passive AI solving.
impact_evidence: Three-level co-op structure and human/agent mutual dependence are clearly described.
Puzzle design explicitly requires communication and waiting.
creativity_rationale: Making an AI agent player two, and designing the missing human-control tool as the core constraint, is exceptionally original and memorable for the medium.
creativity_evidence: The project inverts the usual agent-does-the-chore framing into co-op play.
Solver rejects levels solvable with the robot frozen, demonstrating depth of concept.
usability_note: The constrained co-op premise is legible, but no visual gameplay evidence limits confidence in polish and onboarding.
red_flags: No video frame sheets and only one packaging screenshot; core play is unobserved.
standouts: The absence of a human-control tool is an excellent, principled mechanic.
advance_reason: Exceptional creativity and transformative WebMCP role outweigh thin execution evidence.

one_line: A Wikipedia reader that lets an agent hide spoiler sentences according to the reader's watched history while preserving the original article.
what_it_does: Agent reads article and reader context, writes sentence-level spoiler rules into the page, explains each decision, and lets the reader override hidden content.
leverage_rationale: The page knows article structure while the agent knows reader history and preferences; persistent shared rules across linked articles create a collaboration that a generic one-shot summarizer cannot reproduce comparably.
leverage_evidence: Transcript describes 49 season-specific sentences opened in one call, ordered reasons, persistent rules, and reader override.
Frames show article-reading workspace, instruction/chat areas, and policy/sidebar controls.
Description explicitly frames the intersection of page knowledge and reader knowledge as the core WebMCP fit.
execution_rationale: Transcript and frames together show the complete interaction from article loading through agent decisions, sentence-level masking, persistent policy, and override; no visible final defect is apparent.
execution_evidence: Video transcript explicitly reports article reading, hidden sentence counts, reasons, override, and linked-article persistence.
Frames show a Wikipedia-like document with policy controls and changing document states.
Devpost packaging presents the same Unspoiled reader concept.
impact_rationale: Readers partway through films, series, or books have a specific real desire to access reference information without unwanted endings; preserving the source page addresses it directly.
impact_evidence: Description identifies Wikipedia's lack of spoiler warnings and the need to look up facts mid-story.
Transcript demonstrates season-aware filtering and user override.
creativity_rationale: Sentence-level, persistent, overridable spoiler governance that preserves the source rather than summarizing it is a genuinely novel interaction model and is pursued deeply.
creativity_evidence: Agent writes labels and reasons into the page without printing withheld text.
Policy persists to linked articles and neither page nor agent alone decides spoilers.
usability_note: Visible counts, reasons, and override preserve agency; the policy model may require careful explanation.
standouts: Excellent division of knowledge between page and agent; unusually clear video evidence.
advance_reason: Outstanding leverage, creativity, impact, and evidenced central workflow.

one_line: A read-only FPL planning workspace for hypothetical transfers, lineup experiments, and agent-assisted squad analysis.
what_it_does: Loads public FPL data, validates transfer and formation rules locally, and lets human and agent edit shared drafts without touching the real team.
leverage_rationale: Structured draft and rule tools reduce friction for complex lineup/transfer planning, but a competent general agent could achieve much of the same through the visible planner with real but bounded friction.

execution_evidence: Description specifies Next.js/React/TypeScript, live FPL API, four seasons of local history, and rule validation.
No frame sheets or video submitted; Devpost screenshot is packaging only.

Historical analysis and complete local rule modelling broaden the interaction beyond simple transfers.
usability_note: Read-only drafts are a safe and useful model, but no product frames are available to assess clarity.
red_flags: No public repo, gallery images, video, or frame sheets; execution and eligibility remain weakly evidenced.
standouts: Good safety boundary between hypothetical drafts and the real FPL team.

one_line: A scientific resilience-analysis app where agents and humans share typed analytical state and auditable evidence.
what_it_does: Configures datasets and methods, runs coupling/fragility analysis, inspects withdrawal envelopes and drivers, and offers bounded interpretation and exportable evidence.
leverage_rationale: Typed analytical tools expose domain operations and preserve the exact human-edited scientific state for agent continuation; generic UI driving would be brittle for this multi-step analysis.
leverage_evidence: Description lists eight typed tools, explicit validation, shared in-page state, and human-to-agent handoff.

execution_evidence: About text names outputs including lambda, Phi, rolling rates, stress envelope, drivers, confidence, limitations, and export.

impact_evidence: Description identifies brittle agent interaction with rich analytical apps as the problem.

creativity_rationale: Applying WebMCP to a live scientific state with human revision and evidence-bounded interpretation is an ambitious, original agent interaction beyond generic analytics automation.
creativity_evidence: Human can change method/window/column roles and ask the agent to continue from that exact revised state.
Environmental-withdrawal stress envelope and limitations are first-class outputs.
usability_note: The analytical contract is promising but likely demanding; no screenshots are available to judge the interface.
red_flags: No gallery images or video/frame evidence; visual claims cannot be checked.
standouts: Strong scientific reproducibility and evidence-bounded agent framing.
advance_reason: High leverage and meaningful research impact, despite missing visual evidence.

one_line: A distributor ordering layer that turns messy wholesale language into SKU decisions and asks for clarification instead of guessing.
what_it_does: Resolves each natural-language order line against a 243-SKU catalog, preserves unit mismatches, returns reasons and candidates, and supports agent-operated ordering.
leverage_rationale: Line-level structured resolution, ambiguity handling, and shared catalog state make agent ordering materially more reliable than UI scraping or generic search, though a general agent could approximate some flows.
leverage_evidence: About text specifies resolve_order decisions, exact SKU matching reasons, unit preservation, and clarification candidates.
Frames show natural-language request, line-level matching, partial matches, and ambiguity handling in the browser.
execution_rationale: Video frames and captions demonstrate the central flow from informal order to line matches and clarification, though final checkout/order submission is not shown.
execution_evidence: Frames show 243-SKU catalog context, extracted lines, two immediate matches, and an ambiguous third line.
Description provides concrete SKU 10009 match rationale and charger candidate distinctions.
Devpost packaging aligns with the demonstrated order-entry concept.
impact_rationale: Wholesale buyers and distributor staff face a frequent, concrete cost of manually translating messy order language into catalog SKUs; safe clarification has direct operational value.
impact_evidence: Narrative identifies weekly phone-accessory restocking and 20-minute manual translation per order.
Frames show natural-language input without product codes and per-line catalog matching.
creativity_rationale: The focus on knowing when not to guess, preserving buyer units, and explaining catalog distinctions is a thoughtful and memorable refinement of agent commerce.
creativity_evidence: System returns needs-clarification with actual separating attributes and options.
Buyer language such as cases is recorded rather than silently normalized.
usability_note: Clarification-first behavior and line-level reasons support trust; dense wholesale catalog terminology may remain specialized.
red_flags: Frames do not show a completed placed order or checkout outcome.
standouts: Excellent ambiguity handling and evidence-rich matching rationale.
advance_reason: Strong practical impact and well-demonstrated structured agent workflow.

one_line: An EPUB reader that helps readers untangle difficult literary syntax without replacing the original prose with a summary.
what_it_does: Lets an agent mark sentence spines, unfold nested clauses, reorder syntax, and optionally give plain meaning while keeping the source sentence central.
leverage_rationale: The structured sentence-level operations are more precise and repeatable than asking a general agent for an explanation, and they preserve shared reading context; however, a general agent could provide a comparable explanation with friction.
leverage_evidence: Description specifies four progressive WebMCP operations on the highlighted sentence.
Frame sheets show a document reader/editor with assistant prompts, long-form prose, highlighted passages, and response controls.
execution_rationale: The product concept and visible reading workflow are coherent, but the packet lacks readable final syntax annotations or a clear completed transformation state, so end-to-end execution is capped.
execution_evidence: Frames show EPUB-like reading surface, highlighted text, chat/instruction area, and contextual sidebar.
About text describes progressive hints, but the supplied contact sheets do not clearly expose the resulting spine/reordered syntax.
No video transcript and packaging screenshot is not runtime proof.
impact_rationale: Readers of difficult literature have a specific need for syntax help that does not discard style, rhythm, or original wording; the approach directly serves that need.
impact_evidence: Proust example distinguishes syntax difficulty from vocabulary and rejects summaries.
Feature set escalates assistance while retaining the original sentence.
creativity_rationale: Treating literary comprehension as progressive structural scaffolding rather than summarization is a fresh and well-motivated interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Spine, nested-clause unfolding, familiar-order rearrangement, and optional plain meaning form a deliberate escalation.
Original prose remains the center of the reading experience.
usability_note: Progressive hints are promising for readers, though the visible contact sheets do not make the final transformations legible.
red_flags: Vision evidence for the final syntax operations is limited by contact-sheet resolution and missing transcript.
standouts: Strong anti-summary philosophy and progressive literary scaffolding.
advance_reason: Distinctive education/reading use case with meaningful structured assistance, despite incomplete result evidence.
